entries.title: The Shared Clipboard Inside the Sandbox: Cross-Account Data Leakage in ChatGPT
entries.description: Over the past several years, AI assistants have moved far beyond text generation. Modern systems can execute code, install additional dependencies, analyze user files, and access data through connected services. These capabilities significantly increase the practical value of LLMs, but they also change the security model: protecting user data now depends both on the behavior of the model itself and on its execution environment, the tools available to it, and the platform’s internal services.

entries.description: This article guides readers through establishing an Okta threat detection lab, emphasizing the importance of securing SaaS platforms like Okta. It details creating a lab environment with the Elastic Stack, integrating SIEM solutions, and Okta.

entries.title: STIXy Situations: ECSaping your threat data
entries.description: Structured threat data is commonly formatted using STIX. To help get this data into Elasticsearch, we’re releasing a Python script that converts STIX to an ECS format to be ingested into your stack.

entries.title: Starter guide to understanding Okta
entries.description: This article delves into Okta's architecture and services, laying a solid foundation for threat research and detection engineering. Essential reading for those aiming to master threat hunting and detection in Okta environments.

entries.title: Google Cloud for Cyber Data Analytics
entries.description: This article explains how we conduct comprehensive cyber threat data analysis using Google Cloud, from data extraction and preprocessing to trend analysis and presentation. It emphasizes the value of BigQuery, Python, and Google Sheets - showcasing how to refine and visualize data for insightful cybersecurity analysis.

entries.title: Streamlining ES|QL Query and Rule Validation: Integrating with GitHub CI
entries.description: ES|QL is Elastic's new piped query language. Taking full advantage of this new feature, Elastic Security Labs walks through how to run validation of ES|QL rules for the Detection Engine.

entries.title: Using LLMs and ESRE to find similar user sessions
entries.description: In our previous article, we explored using the GPT-4 Large Language Model (LLM) to condense Linux user sessions. In the context of the same experiment, we dedicated some time to examine sessions that shared similarities. These similar sessions can subsequently aid the analysts in identifying related suspicious activities.

entries.title: Using LLMs to summarize user sessions
entries.description: In this publication, we will talk about lessons learned and key takeaways from our experiments using GPT-4 to summarize user sessions.

entries.title: Forget vulnerable drivers - Admin is all you need
entries.description: Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) is an increasingly popular attacker technique whereby a threat actor brings a known-vulnerable signed driver alongside their malware, loads it into the kernel, then exploits it to perform some action within the kernel that they would not otherwise be able to do. Employed by advanced threat actors for over a decade, BYOVD is becoming increasingly common in ransomware and commodity malware.

entries.title: Detect domain generation algorithm (DGA) activity with new Kibana integration
entries.description: We have added a DGA detection package to the Integrations app in Kibana. In a single click, you can install and start using the DGA model and associated assets, including ingest pipeline configurations, anomaly detection jobs, and detection rules.

entries.title: Unpacking ICEDID
entries.description: ICEDID is known to pack its payloads using custom file formats and a custom encryption scheme. We are releasing a set of tools to automate the unpacking process and help analysts and the community respond to ICEDID.

entries.title: Click, Click… Boom! Automating Protections Testing with Detonate
entries.description: To automate this process and test our protections at scale, we built Detonate, a system that is used by security research engineers to measure the efficacy of our Elastic Security solution in an automated fashion.

entries.title: Exploring the Future of Security with ChatGPT
entries.description: Recently, OpenAI announced APIs for engineers to integrate ChatGPT and Whisper models into their apps and products. For some time, engineers could use the REST API calls for older models and otherwise use the ChatGPT interface through their website.

entries.title: Elastic Global Threat Report Multipart Series Overview
entries.description: Each month, the Elastic Security Labs team dissects a different trend or correlation from the Elastic Global Threat Report. This post provides an overview of those individual publications.

entries.title: Hunting for Suspicious Windows Libraries for Execution and Defense Evasion
entries.description: Learn more about discovering threats by hunting through DLL load events, one way to reveal the presence of known and unknown malware in noisy process event data.

entries.title: The Elastic Container Project for Security Research
entries.description: The Elastic Container Project provides a single shell script that will allow you to stand up and manage an entire Elastic Stack using Docker. This open source project enables rapid deployment for testing use cases.

entries.title: Stopping Vulnerable Driver Attacks
entries.description: This post includes a primer on kernel mode attacks, along with Elastic’s recommendations for securing users from kernel attacks leveraging vulnerable drivers.

entries.title: Identifying beaconing malware using Elastic
entries.description: In this blog, we walk users through identifying beaconing malware in their environment using our beaconing identification framework.

entries.title: Hunting for Lateral Movement using Event Query Language
entries.description: Elastic Event Query Language (EQL) correlation capabilities enable practitioners to capture complex behavior for adversary Lateral Movement techniques. Learn how to detect a variety of such techniques in this blog post.

entries.title: Detecting Living-off-the-land attacks with new Elastic Integration
entries.description: We added a Living off the land (LotL) detection package to the Integrations app in Kibana. In a single click, you can install and start using the ProblemChild model and associated assets including anomaly detection configurations and detection rules.

entries.title: Detect Credential Access with Elastic Security
entries.description: Elastic Endpoint Security provides events that enable defenders with visibility on techniques and procedures which are commonly leveraged to access sensitive files and registry objects.

entries.title: Ingesting threat data with the Threat Intel Filebeat module
entries.description: Tutorial that walks through setting up Filebeat to push threat intelligence feeds into your Elastic Stack.

entries.title: Automating the Security Protections rapid response to malware
entries.description: See how we’ve been improving the processes that allow us to make updates quickly in response to new information and propagate those protections to our users, with the help of machine learning models.

entries.title: NETWIRE Dynamic Configuration Extraction
entries.description: Elastic Security Labs discusses the NETWIRE trojan and is releasing a tool to dynamically extract configuration files.

entries.title: NETWIRE Configuration Extractor
entries.description: Python script to extract the configuration from NETWIRE samples.

entries.title: Vulnerability summary: Follina, CVE-2022-30190
entries.description: Elastic is deploying a new malware signature to identify the use of the Follina vulnerability. Learn more in this post.

entries.title: Elastic’s 2022 Global Threat Report: A roadmap for navigating today’s growing threatscape
entries.description: Threat intelligence resources like the 2022 Elastic Global Threat Report are critical to helping teams evaluate their organizational visibility, capabilities, and expertise in identifying and preventing cybersecurity threats.

entries.title: QBOT Configuration Extractor
entries.description: Python script to extract the configuration from QBOT samples.

entries.title: ICEDID Configuration Extractor
entries.description: Python script to extract the configuration from ICEDID samples.

entries.title: BPFDoor Configuration Extractor
entries.description: Configuration extractor to dump out hardcoded passwords with BPFDoor.

entries.title: PARALLAX Payload Extractor
entries.description: Python script to extract the payload from PARALLAX samples.

entries.title: BPFDoor Scanner
entries.description: Python script to identify hosts infected with the BPFDoor malware.
